# dsh-plugin-mobile-gateway
> **v0.12.0 · pending release** — Targets DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 and Node.js 24.9+. Adds ordered chat quotes
, Host-wide schedule management, plugin updates and details, and a language selector that follows DS
H. Fixes batched projection updates and image reads. See the changelog and mobile integration guide.
> Current source adds experimental **P2P-first** transport. With `webrtc.enabled: true`, compatible
clients negotiate two WebRTC DataChannels over the existing authenticated WebSocket and fall back as
a group to WebSocket. First use defaults to LAN direct over WebSocket on the same Wi-Fi. Opt into a
P2P or other connection plan under Connection & Pairing; saved choices are preserved. Existing clie
nts are unchanged. **Gateway ready for integration; Android/iOS integration and device acceptance ar
e pending. Not released.** See the client contract, runtime decision, and acceptance record.
A third-party mobile gateway for DeepSeek Harness with device authentication. Supports sessions and
live events; queued-message synchronization, editing, deletion, and Steer; bidirectional session arc
hiving and renaming; stopping and resuming generation; task lists and the current Goal; server-drive
n command and skill menus; human-in-the-loop workflows; and image and file transfers. After installa
tion, a Mobile Devices entry appears in the Harness WebUI sidebar for enabling the gateway, generati
ng pairing QR codes, and managing trusted devices.
> The current source targets **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1**, requires the Connection Peer interface, and uses Se

ssion format 4. Older history cursors require a fresh baseline.

## Protocol and DSH Compatibility Layer
Mobile clients use this project's `dsh-mobile-v1`, not DSH's internal Remote protocol. A separate Ho
st Adapter connects to the DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 Remote Gateway. Namespaces such as Session, Workspace, Set
tings, Commands, Goals, Schedule, Permission Presets, and Plugin Manager, together with their strict
parameters, are confined to that adapter. See the RC2 plugin management integration plan for reques
t frames and mobile UI design.
DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 requires `peer` on every Remote call. The gateway creates a local-user Peer with `ctx
.connection.createPeer()` and disposes of it with the plugin. The Host Adapter injects it into regul
ar requests, initial reads, and live subscriptions; mobile clients cannot choose the caller identity
. Questions and approvals still use the gateway's Host listeners. Older gateways that omit it fail w
ith `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'signal')`. After upgrading DSH, reinstall this so
urce version and restart `dsh web`; the phone protocol needs no change.

s services, no user sessions read or written):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Pairing authentication and `dsh-mobile-v1` / `hello.protocol = 3` are unchanged. Live tokens no long
er consume persistent event `seq` values: explicitly subscribe with `assistantStream: true` to recei
ve an atomic `session-snapshot` and separate deltas. Regular `event` frames contain only persistent
events. Clients without the new subscription receive persistent messages only.
History responses include `historyFormatVersion` and `cursor`. Clear history caches and install a fr
esh baseline when the format changes. Pagination with `beforeSeq` or a fork with `atSeq` must also s

end `historyFormatVersion: 4`.
See the rc.2 mobile integration guide for current integration and acc
eptance checks, and the Remote Gateway refactoring plan for earlier migration records.

- WebSocket: `/ws/mobile`
- LAN: `ws://<局域网 IP>:3081/ws/mobile`
- Public Linux server: `wss://<公网 IP

>/ws/mobile`

## Multi-Gateway Phase One (Current Source)
Provides a stable `gatewayId`, configurable `gatewayName`, pairing endpoint candidates, and persiste
nt Off / Temporary / Persistent modes. One app can pair independently with gateways on different mac
hines; client-side multi-gateway management must implement the integration guide. No new npm version
has been published for this source change.
Choose Persistent in Mobile Devices to continue accepting authorized devices across restarts. DSH mu
st remain running, the host awake, and the network reachable. This does not provide automatic discov
ery or a network relay.
Example deployment settings (the mobile-gateway plugin's `config`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Mode precedence: **saved UI selection > `gatewayMode` > legacy `gatewayEnabled`**. Without a saved s
election, legacy `gatewayEnabled: true` means Persistent; false means Off.

- Off: disconnects mobile devices immediately and stays off after restart.
- Temporary: switches off
and saves Off if no device connects successfully within 5 minutes by default. After a successful co
nnection it stays on for that run. Restarting in Temporary mode restarts the wait. `gatewayWaitTimeo

utMs` allows 30 seconds to 30 minutes.
- Persistent: no idle waiting timer. Pairing codes still expi
re after 5 minutes by default; file-transfer timeouts and other independent rules are unchanged.
State defaults to `<deviceFile>.gateway.json`, usually `~/.dsh/mobile-gateway-devices.json.gateway.j
son`, or a configured `gatewayStateFile`. It holds a random UUID v4 identity and user selections, ha
s mode `0600`, and is atomically replaced using a temporary file in the same directory. Corruption f
ails startup rather than silently generating a new identity. Each running instance needs separate de
vice registry and state files.
